requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]` covers the obligations of `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`.

**Stop when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive failure**
- The main loop feeds repeated 429 `ThrottlingException` failures to `ProviderBackoff::retry`, advancing `now` by each returned delay. It asserts that no attempt is scheduled after `start + 60s`. It also asserts that the loop eventually stops, after more than 3 attempts.
- An implementation that never stops, or that measures from the last failure instead of the first, would fail this loop.
- A boundary case checks a second failure at 58s. It must still wait, with a delay of at most 2s.
- `Retry-After` at the limit is parameterized. A value of "60" must wait exactly 60s, because that is not more than a minute. A value of "61" must stop.
- A `Retry-After` of "90" stops at once. This covers "including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point".
- Under the 58s case, a stop that fires before the limit would be caught.

**Error naming the number of attempts and the last failure's HTTP status and code, when available**
- The main loop's message must contain "after {attempts+1} attempts". This is the count of `retry` calls, and the message also contains "kept failing for a minute".
- The same message must contain "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException", which covers status and code together.
- A parameterized case covers the "when available" variants. Status only gives "last failure: HTTP 503". Code only gives "last failure: ThrottlingException". Neither, in a timeout error, gives "last failure: no response within ten minutes". Each case also asserts that the error kind is `TimedOut`.

**Permanent errors**
- A 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error, not the "kept failing" error. This checks that the limit is only for transient failures.

**Out of scope or not needed here**
- Retry classification, backoff doubling, jitter and the reset after success belong to the parent `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`. They are covered by other tests such as `retries_throttling_unavailability_and_timeouts_but_not_permanent_errors`.
- I read `ProviderBackoff::retry` only to see how the limit is applied. The harness's `converse` just returns `AgentError::Provider(error)` on `Retry::Stop`. That is a pass-through and needs no separate test.

I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST count toward the assessment totals under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
